En la fila **Language** (Idioma), haz clic y selecciona **Español (Latinoamérica)**.

🎉 **¡Listo!** Toda la interfaz se adaptará de inmediato a español latinoamericano y la preferencia quedará guardada de forma permanente para tus próximas sesiones. --- ## ⚡ Instalación alternativa por terminal (CLI) Si prefieres instalarlo mediante la línea de comandos de `dsh`: ### Para la interfaz Web: ```bash # Mediante enlace directo al repositorio: git clone https://github.com/Dreftian/dsh-locale-es-419.git cd dsh-locale-es-419 dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd) ``` En **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/Dreftian/dsh-locale-es-419.git cd dsh-locale-es-419 dsh plugin --profile web add link:(Get-Location).Path ``` ### Para la aplicación Desktop: ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:$(pwd) ``` En **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:(Get-Location).Path ``` --- ## 🌟 Características clave | Característica | Detalle | |---|---| | **Estándar BCP 47 (`es-419`)** | Reconocimiento automático para navegadores y sistemas operativos de Latinoamérica (México, Colombia, Argentina, Perú, Chile, etc.). | | **Terminología neutra** | Vocabulario natural para la región: *archivo*, *computadora*, *configuración*, *guardar*, *cancelar*, *detener*. | | **58 Módulos cubiertos** | Cobertura integral: chat, workspace, terminal, modelos, configuración, atajos de teclado, subagentes y herramientas. | | **Fallback resiliente a inglés (`en`)** | Cualquier función nueva o texto pendiente recurre de forma segura a inglés, evitando errores en la UI. | | **Persistencia duradera** | Tu selección se guarda en `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` bajo la clave `locale.preference`. | --- ## 🤝 Cómo contribuir ¡Las contribuciones de toda la comunidad hispanohablante son bienvenidas! 1. Los diccionarios editables están en [`locale/es-419/*.json`](locale/es-419/). 2. Reconstruye el paquete con: ```bash npm run build ``` 3. Envía un Pull Request con tus mejoras y ajustes de traducción. --- ## 🌐 English **dsh-locale-es-419** is an open-source community language pack plugin providing Latin American Spanish (`es-419`) localization for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). ### Quick Install In DeepSeek Harness: 1. Go to **Plugins** → **+ Add plugin**. 2. Enter: ```text https://github.com/Dreftian/dsh-locale-es-419 ``` 3. Click **Install**. 4. Open **Settings → General → Language** and pick **Español (Latinoamérica)**. --- ## 📄 Licencia [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Dangelo Vilchez ([@Dreftian](https://github.com/Dreftian))

plugins.description: OpenChamber-style handoff review for DeepSeek Harness: linked read-only review sessions, round by round.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-handoff-review

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) plugin that hands the
current session's changes to a linked, **read-only review session** — a
round-by-round handoff review in the spirit of OpenChamber.

The implementation session keeps working; an ordinary review session in the same
workspace reviews the change in an independent context. Its report can be sent
back to the implementer, later revisions can be sent back to the reviewer, and
every round is kept in a durable link record. The plugin only adds commands,
routes, projections, listeners and UI slots: nothing is written into the DSH
kernel, and removing the bundle removes everything it registered.

![Handoff review panel](docs/screenshots/panel.png)

*Link state, both sessions, actions and round history in the right-sidebar
panel (session and link ids masked).*

![Handoff review settings](docs/screenshots/settings.png)

*Reviewer route and handoff limits under Settings → Handoff Review.*

## Features

- **One command to start.** `/handoff-review focus on retry logic` (or the
  composer dock button) creates or reuses a link, opens a review session and
  delivers a handoff brief: goal, review focus, changed files, unified diff,
  verification and open questions.
- **Read-only reviewer.** Three independent layers: a durable
  `sandbox/mode: read-only` session event, removal/denial of write tools on the
  reviewer's scoped tool runtime, and an `approval: never` policy.
- **Round loop.** Send the reviewer's report back to the implementation session;
  after the fixes, send only the changes after the last handoff watermark as
  round + 1. `maxRounds`, per-round dedupe and a delivery rate limit keep the
  loop bounded.
- **Panel and history.** Right-sidebar panel with link state, both sessions with
  real navigation, expandable round history, handoff/report previews, a
  changed-files diff drawer, and multi-link selection in the dock.
- **Optional auto-continue.** Start the review once and reports/revisions are
  delivered automatically when each turn ends, until a stop condition (see
  below).
- **Configurable reviewer.** Provider, model, thinking effort and agent preset,
  picked from the installed catalog.
- **Localized UI.** English and Traditional Chinese, light/dark via theme
  tokens.

## Requirements

- DSH Desktop (`0.2.x`) with `ctx.storageDomain` available (the stock `desktop`
  profile satisfies this).
- Node.js >= 20 for development and tests.

## Install

This is a profile bundle with a Host half and a Web Client half. The desktop
profile is managed by the app, so install it through the app:

1. Open **Settings → Plugins → Install bundle**.
2. Enter the absolute path of this directory (or a packed package).
3. Restart DSH Desktop so the new Host/Client generation loads.

The bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) contributes one composition row:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: handoff-review
      name: dsh-handoff-review
      config:
        maxRounds: 3
        maxHandoffChars: 30000
        diffPerFileChars: 6000
```

## Use

1. Work in an implementation session until it has `edit`/`write` changes.
2. Run `/handoff-review focus on retry logic`, or click **Handoff review** in the
   composer dock. The review session appears in the same workspace, titled
   `Review: <impl title> (round N)`.
3. Open the review session and let the reviewer work.
4. When the reviewer finishes, the link becomes `feedback_ready`. In the
   implementation session press **Send feedback** (or run
   `/handoff-review feedback` from the review session).
5. After the fixes, press **Send revision** (or `/handoff-review revision`) — only
   changes after the last handoff watermark are sent, round + 1. Past
   `maxRounds`, the dock offers **Send revision (force)** and the command accepts
   `--force`.
6. Repeat, then press **Close** (or `/handoff-review close`). Sessions are never
   deleted; the review session keeps its history.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/handoff-review [focus]` | create/reuse a link and deliver a handoff |
| `/handoff-review status` | print the current link state |
| `/handoff-review feedback` | send the reviewer's report to the implementer |
| `/handoff-review revision [--force]` | send new changes as the next round |
| `/handoff-review close` | close the link (history is kept) |
| `/handoff-review reopen` | reopen a closed link |
| `/handoff-review --new [focus]` | open another link for the same session |
| `/handoff-review -- <focus>` | escape a focus that starts with a command word |

### Automatic continuation

Enable **Settings → Handoff Review → 行為 → 自動接續審查流程** once. From then on
**starting a review is the only manual action**: when the reviewer turn ends its
report is delivered to the implementation session, and when the implementation
turn ends the new changes are sent back to the reviewer. The loop stops at
`maxRounds` (no automatic `--force`), when there are no new changes, when a peer
session is offline, or when the link is closed. A stop injects a non-waking
`[handoff-review]` notice instead of looping, and automation re-arms on restart
or when a peer session is reopened.

## Settings

Settings are persisted in the plugin's own storage domain
(`handoff_review_settings`) — no profile YAML edits.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `reviewerProvider` / `reviewerModel` | route of the review session | reviewer routing |
| `reviewerReasoningEffort` | model default | thinking level, e.g. `high` |
| `reviewerPreset` | deployment default | agent preset for the review session |
| `maxRounds` | `3` | revisions beyond this need `--force` |
| `autoContinue` | `false` | run the review loop automatically |

The page also exposes `maxHandoffChars` (30000), `diffPerFileChars` (6000),
`autoSummarize` (off), `readOnlyReviewer` (on) and `maxDeliveriesPerMinute` (6).
A saved value applies to new reviews; an existing link keeps the reviewer route
captured when it was created.

## Security

- The reviewer cannot modify files (sandbox mode, tool guard, approval policy).
- Reviewer reports are untrusted data: every cross-session message starts with
  `[handoff-review] …` and marks itself as data, not instructions.
- Credential-looking diff lines (`*_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`, `password`, `secret`,
  `api[_-]?key`) are redacted and `.env`-like files are skipped. A diff can still
  contain sensitive material — treat handoffs like patches.
- `/handoff-review/api/*` are exact web-server routes and apply the host
  browser-trust fence themselves; no approval escalation is performed.

## Development

```bash
pnpm install        # or npm install
npm run check       # node --check on every module
npm test            # node:test unit + integration suite (92 tests)
```

Tests cover the handoff builder, projections, link store, delivery loop breaker,
route fence, command grammar, reviewer lockdown, config admin and a fake-Cordis
round trip (create → feedback → revision → close → reopen).

## Status and limitations

- A review session cannot create another link, so review-of-review chains are
  intentionally blocked.
- No cross-machine sync/relay; no Review button inside the official diff card
  (no public slot — the standalone diff drawer is used instead).
- The UI is localized (en / zh-TW); Host-side command receipts and route errors
  are Traditional Chinese only.

See [`DEVELOPMENT.md`](./DEVELOPMENT.md) for the full specification, assumptions
and as-built notes.

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Xiaoyaoyou glyph-water background for DeepSeek Harness new conversations: flowing text light, ripples, and sparse accents.
plugins.readme_text:
# 逍遥游 · Glyph Water

A DeepSeek Harness visual plugin for the **new conversation screen only**.
Fixed Chinese glyphs form a quiet surface. Their opacity flows like mist;
clicks create outward ripples, with sparse blue accent clusters.

一个只在 **新建会话页** 生效的 DeepSeek Harness 背景插件。
字形固定，明暗流动。点击空白区域会荡开涟漪。
进入已有对话或插件页后，背景自动卸载。

## Screenshots / 效果截图

Two user-provided screenshots, shown as a looping GIF.
Each screenshot stays visible for 2.5 seconds. This is a slideshow,
not a recording of the continuous animation.

使用两张实机截图制作循环 GIF，每张停留 2.5 秒。
这是截图轮播，不是连续动画录屏。

![Two screenshot states of the Xiaoyaoyou glyph-water background](docs/images/preview.gif)

Original images / 原始清晰截图：
[截图一](docs/images/new-conversation.png) · [截图二](docs/images/new-conversation-ripple.png)

## Companion editor / 配套编辑器

[Glyph Studio](https://github.com/Aimer779/glyph-studio) is the standalone
editor behind this plugin. Use its parameter panel to explore text, gradients,
ripples and accent colors. This repository contains the DSH integration.

需要可视化调参时，使用原项目
[字间 · Glyph Studio](https://github.com/Aimer779/glyph-studio)。
它提供文字、渐变、波纹和点缀的参数面板。
导出的参数可写入本插件的 `theme.json`，再重新构建安装。

## Install / 安装

**Tested and declared compatible with DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` only.**
Desktop on Windows was tested. Other versions and platforms are unverified.
The manifest restricts installation to that DSH version.

1. Download `local-dsh-xiaoyaoyou-0.1.0.tgz` from
   [Releases](https://github.com/Aimer779/dsh-xiaoyaoyou/releases/tag/v0.1.0).
2. Open a terminal in the download directory and run:

   ```powershell
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./local-dsh-xiaoyaoyou-0.1.0.tgz
   ```

3. Restart DeepSeek Harness. Open **Plugins** and confirm that
   **逍遥游 · 字间水面 / Xiaoyaoyou · Glyph Water** is enabled.
4. Open a new conversation.

安装包已包含前端构建产物，无需安装时构建。
在下载目录执行上述命令，再重启 DSH。
在插件页确认开关已启用，打开新建会话即可。

The package is distributed through GitHub Releases, **not npm**.
Its package identifier is `@local/dsh-xiaoyaoyou`.
`private: true` prevents accidental npm publication; it does not prevent
installation from the release archive.

Disable it from the Plugins page. To uninstall:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @local/dsh-xiaoyaoyou
```

## Behavior / 效果

- Fixed 18 × 20 px glyph grid, using a passage from Zhuangzi's *Xiaoyaoyou*.
- Flowing opacity fields; glyphs do not translate or jitter.
- Click ripples with a narrow crest and a fading wake.
- Sparse, irregular clusters of accent-colored glyphs.
- Pale radial gradient confined to the new conversation content area.
- Input fields, buttons, menus and links do not trigger ripples.
- Hidden windows pause animation; reduced-motion preference shows a still field.
- Leaving the hero screen releases the canvas, animation and event listeners.

The supplied preset uses propagation speed 1200, idle depth 0.23,
threshold 0.31, and four accent clusters of seven glyphs each.
The original tuning panel is not included in this plugin.

## Customize and build / 修改与构建

Requires Node.js 22 or newer. No package dependencies are required.
React is supplied by the DSH frontend module loader.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Aimer779/dsh-xiaoyaoyou.git
cd dsh-xiaoyaoyou
node build.mjs
node --test test/*.test.cjs
pnpm pack --out local-dsh-xiaoyaoyou-0.1.0.tgz
```

Edit `theme.json`, then rebuild and reinstall the archive.
Do not edit generated `client.js` directly.
No localhost server or original Glyph Studio checkout is needed.

修改 `theme.json` 后，重新构建并安装生成的包。
文字、渐变色、点缀颜色和动画参数都保存在此文件中。

## Integration and limits / 接入边界

The plugin registers through DSH's `window.__ModuleLoader__` and
`shell.overlay` slot. The adapter attaches a decorative layer to:

```css
[data-phase="hero"] [data-conversation-content][data-content-phase="hero"]
```

This semantic DOM contract was verified against the desktop's bundled
`0.2.1-rc.2` frontend. It is not a guaranteed public background-slot API.
If DSH changes that contract, the adapter must be updated.
If no matching node exists, the plugin displays nothing.

There are no agent tools, network requests, telemetry or conversation-text reads.
The decoration uses `aria-hidden` and does not capture pointer events.
It does not modify DSH's application files or global theme settings.

## Verification / 验证

Verified on 2026-10-18:

- New conversation: glyph field and click ripple visible.
- Existing conversation and Plugins page: no plugin background.
- Return to new conversation: background returns.
- Automated lifecycle tests: mount once, unmount, dispose, pause when hidden,
  reduced motion, and no restart from deferred font readiness after disposal.

No test message was sent to a model. The first-send transition was not tested
end to end; its lifecycle state change is covered by the adapter tests.
Other DSH releases, dark mode, platforms and the Web profile are unverified.

## Source and license

Effect algorithms originated in [Glyph Studio](https://github.com/Aimer779/glyph-studio).
The classical Chinese passage is public-domain text.
Plugin code: [MIT](LICENSE).

DSH references:
[plugin packaging guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md),
[community contribution guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).

plugins.description: Expose a stdio MCP server (Playwright, Chrome DevTools, any MCP) as native DeepSeek Harness tools
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-mcp-bridge

Expose **any stdio MCP server** as native DeepSeek Harness tools. Host-only plugin, no browser UI, no npm dependencies.

Built for one job: let a DSH agent drive a browser through the official **Microsoft Playwright MCP** server, attached to the Edge/Chrome you are already using.

## What it does

1. On load, spawns the MCP server once (default `npx --yes @playwright/mcp@latest --cdp-endpoint=msedge`).
2. Calls `initialize` + `tools/list`, converts each tool's JSON Schema into a DSH parameter schema, and registers it with `ctx.tools.register`.
3. Every tool call is forwarded as `tools/call`; the result is returned as JSON. Images (screenshots) are written to a temp file and returned as a path, not as base64.

Tools are renamed: `browser_navigate` becomes `edge_navigate` (prefix configurable).

## Default tool set (12 of Playwright's 25)

`edge_navigate`, `edge_navigate_back`, `edge_snapshot`, `edge_click`, `edge_type`, `edge_fill_form`, `edge_press_key`, `edge_tabs`, `edge_take_screenshot`, `edge_evaluate`, `edge_wait_for`, `edge_close`.

The full set costs prompt space in every session, which is why it is not the default. Set `MCP_BRIDGE_ALL=1` to expose everything.

## Install

```powershell
cd E:\dsh
.\rollback.cmd guard add "file:C:\path\to\dsh-mcp-bridge"
.\rollback.cmd health
```

Restart DSH (or rely on hot-load) and open a new session.

## Configuration

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MCP_BRIDGE_COMMAND` | `npx --yes @playwright/mcp@latest --cdp-endpoint=msedge` | The MCP server command line (any stdio MCP server) |
| `MCP_BRIDGE_PREFIX` | `edge` | Tool name prefix |
| `MCP_BRIDGE_ALL` | unset | `1` = register every tool the server offers |
| `MCP_BRIDGE_TOOLS` | unset | Comma-separated allow-list of MCP tool names |
| `MCP_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT` | `120000` | Per-call timeout (ms) |
| `MCP_BRIDGE_INIT_TIMEOUT` | `30000` | Startup timeout (ms) |

## Prerequisite for the Edge/Chrome you are already using

Open `edge://inspect/#remote-debugging` (or `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`) and enable **Allow remote debugging for this browser instance**. Then `--cdp-endpoint=msedge` (or `=chrome`) attaches to that running browser with your logins and extensions. Without the toggle, Playwright launches a fresh browser instead.

## Failure behaviour

If the MCP server cannot start or does not answer, the plugin **registers nothing and logs the reason** — it never throws, so it cannot take the host boot down. Check `MCP_BRIDGE_INIT_TIMEOUT` and the stderr tail printed in the DSH console.

## Privacy

The bridge itself makes no network calls. It spawns exactly one child process (the MCP server you configured) and forwards bytes between it and the tool call. With `--cdp-endpoint`, the MCP server attaches to your existing browser, which means it can see and act on the tabs you have open — treat that as giving the agent your browser session.

## License

MIT.

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

## Where it fits — and the goal

Engramory is a **portable memory *discipline*, not a

plugins.description: dsh 插件：AI 选择题自动加一项「幸运方块」随机决定 + 说「回滚」撤销；界面上的骰子按钮长按挖穿即触发随机事件（写论文/我的世界概念合成/冷笑话/冷知识/时事新闻/弹窗表演/蓝屏屏保），整体致敬《赛博朋克 2077》的四季宝
plugins.readme_text:
# 幸运方块 (dsh-lucky-block)

一个 dsh 插件，同时工作在 dsh web 与 dsh desktop。两件事：

1. **幸运方块选项** —— AI 向你提选择题时，每个问题的选项末尾会自动多出一个「幸运方块」。
   选它，就随机替你挑一个选项、或把几个选项揉成一个新方案，全随机。
   不满意？说一句「回滚」（或打 `/rollback`），立刻回到上一版本。
2. **幸运方块按钮** —— 屏幕角落一个可拖动、可锁定的我的世界幸运方块（16×16 原版方块面贴图）。
   闲着没事就戳它一下：**左键单点**零成本，抽弹窗表演 / 假蓝屏 / 今日运气 / 冷知识 / 冷笑话；
   **长按** 1.4 秒挖穿它，伴随裂纹、碎裂粒子和原版 Minecraft 挖石头声，接着它会在你的
   默认工作区自动开一个新会话，**全程不需要你做任何事**地随机写篇论文 / 扒几条新闻 / 整理待办。
   松手时方块若离屏幕边缘够近（48px 以内）会**自动吸附贴边**。

它会说话。所有随机事件都套着一层固定的说话腔调：短句、机器口吻、偶尔损你一句。
这套腔调是纯文本的，参数在 `lib/persona.js` 的 `DEFAULT_PERSONA` 里，
可以用配置里的 `persona` 整段换成你自己写的性格。
它**从不往会话里写东西**，所以绝不会污染你的对话历史。

## 两个池：单击零成本，长按才花钱

脚本现在分成**两个互相独立的池**，触发方式不同，抽的东西也不同：

| 触发 | 代价 | 池 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **左键单点** | 零 token、零延迟、**不建会话** | 弹窗 / 蓝屏 / 抽签 / 冷知识 / 冷笑话 |
| **长按挖满**（1.4 秒） | 开新会话、调模型 | 论文 / 新闻 / 待办整理 |

单点是手滑也会发生的动作，所以它不该有成本；长按是明确意图，才值得花 token。
分成两个池而不是一个池加过滤，是为了让两边的权重能独立调节 —— 否则往单击池
里加十条音频，会把长按事件的命中率一起稀释掉。

### 单击池（5 个事件，权重合计 14）

| 概率 | 事件 | 类型 | 会做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14.3% | 无害弹窗表演 | 视觉 | 界面上连弹 24 个无意义提示框，再按创建顺序倒序全部关掉 |
| 14.3% | 蓝屏屏保（60 秒） | 视觉 | 全屏显示一份仿 Windows 蓝屏，60 秒后自动恢复，按 ESC 提前结束 |
| 21.4% | 抽今日运气 | 本地 | 抽一档签文：鸿运齐天 / 大吉 / 中吉 / 小吉 / 平 / 凶。**不调 AI**，附「无科学依据，仅供参考」 |
| 28.6% | 随机冷知识闲聊 | 本地 | 从 818 条本地冷知识库里抽 1~3 条，一次说完 |
| 21.4% | 冷笑话专场 | 本地 | 从 353 条本地笑话库里抽 1~2 条 |

### 长按池（3 个事件，权重合计 8）

| 概率 | 事件 | 类型 | 会做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 37.5% | 随机选题写论文 | AI | 随机词条拼出题目（如「边缘计算 × 古籍数字化 × 的鲁棒性研究」），写 4 节正文并落盘到 `lucky-block-papers/<hash>.md` |
| 37.5% | 时事新闻速览 | AI | **联网**检索 3 条最近真实新闻，每条一句事实 + 一句点评 + 来源链接；查不到就直说，绝不编 |
| 25.0% | 随机整理待办 | AI | 列出工作区最近改的 5 个文件，随机分「紧急 / 不紧急」并明说自己不可信 |

**单击池五个全部零 token、不建会话、零延迟** —— 点下去立刻有反应。

「抽今日运气」**一天只抽一次**：当天再点，返回的还是那一签，并在末尾注明
「今天已经抽过了，明天再来吧。」。状态记在
`$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-lucky-block/fortune-state.json`，删掉这个文件就等于当天重抽。

「抽今日运气」的签文权重是刻意偏吉的：**吉类合计 90%**（鸿运齐天 5% / 大吉 26% /
中吉 33% / 小吉 26%），平 9.9%，凶只有 **0.1%**；
而且**「凶」的正文是反着写的**（「从某种角度来说，你运气还挺好 —— 今天该踩的坑都提前踩完了」），
抽到下签也能笑一下。这个插件是用来打发时间的，不是用来给人添堵的。

### 音频事件（骨架已就位，等清单）

`lib/audio-tracks.json` 现在是空数组，对应的事件权重为 0、不参与抽取。
以后往这个 json 里填 `{ "file": "xxx.ogg", "title": "显示名" }`，
把文件丢进 `lib/audio/`，事件就自动开始参与抽取 —— **不用改代码**。
文件名只接受 `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` + `.ogg|.mp3`，防目录穿越。

### 骰子会话里你只会看到一行字

开新会话的那 3 个事件，**用户消息只有一行**（`🎲 随机事件：时事新闻速览`），
人格设定和任务正文走的是**系统提示**，不会糊在你眼前。

这样做纯粹是为了观感 —— 之前用户消息里塞着几百字的指令墙，点进会话第一眼就是它。
需要说明的是，宿主没有「发一条不显示的消息」这种能力（`PromptContentPart` 只有
text / image / file 三种，没有任何可见性字段），所以这里不是把消息藏起来，
而是**根本不把它发成消息**。

清单可用 `node tools/list-events.mjs` 随时重新生成 —— 它直接从 `lib/index.js`
的 `buildEvents()` 里解析并按池分组，不会和代码漂移。

## 设置面板（右键方块 → 设置…）

| 开关 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| 长按挖掘音效 | 循环挖掘声 + 碎裂声。关掉就完全静音 |

面板里还列着事件清单，每条事件标着它属于**单击**还是**长按** ——
照着这张表就知道点一下会发生什么、要不要花 token。

冷知识和冷笑话现在**固定走本地库**，不再有「调不调 AI」的开关：
它们本来就在单击池里，单击不该有成本，给一个勾选框只会让人以为这里能省钱。

| 本地库 | 条数 | 位置 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 冷笑话 + 点评 | 353 条 + 30 条 | `lib/jokes-data.json` |
| 冷知识 | 818 条（人体 133 / 动物 139 / 科学 121 / 日常 111 / 历史 111 / 地理 103 / 语言 100） | `lib/trivia-data.json` |

冷知识库里分主题存的 `topic` **只用于统计，永远不显示给用户** —— 显示主题等于
把「这是一条从哪抽的」直接摊开。笑话的 `form` 字段同理。

两个库的**完整内容**可以在 [`lib/语料库总览.md`](<lib/语料库总览.md>) 里逐条翻阅；
那份文件由 `node tools/build-corpus-overview.mjs` 从运行库生成，改动语料后重跑即可
（`--check` 用于回归时校验它没过期）。

写进配置也会被忽略并记一条警告。

设置写在 `%DSH_HOME%\plugins\dsh-lucky-block\config.json`，是**手写与界面共用的同一个文件**
（界面保存走读-改-写，不会抹掉你手写的 `model` / `persona`）：

```json
{
  "sound": true,
  "model": { "provider": "workbuddy", "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "reasoningEffort": "low" }
}
```

`localOnly` 已经没有了 —— 冷知识/冷笑话现在无条件走本地库，见上面「设置面板」一节。
老配置里留着这个字段不会报错，只是被忽略。

## 安装（本地开发）

```bash
# 方式一：直接指向本目录（plugin-manager 支持本地 spec）
#   在插件市场里「安装」填本目录的绝对路径

# 方式二：npm 打包后按包装
npm pack
```

装完后**不需要**动 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`：宿主侧条目由本包
`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 自动插入，profile 的 patch 里再加一条同 id 的
`- insert:` 反而会造成组装冲突、让插件加载不上（实测踩过）。

只要确认 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里有
`"dsh-lucky-block"`（插件市场安装会自动加；手动装则加这一行）。

`"patchReload": "live"`（profile 自带）让 `cordis.patch.yml` 热生效；但**改动
`bundles` 列表必须重启 dsh**才生效。

> ⚠️ **改 `lib/` 下的任何 JS 都必须重启 dsh。** 宿主侧插件代码没有热重载 ——
> 正在跑的进程内存里持有旧模块，代码改了行为不会变。这个坑骗过一整轮排查：
> 源码里已经搜不到某段字符串，会话里却还在出现它，最后才发现是进程跑的是旧代码。
> 客户端那半（`lib/client.js`）刷新页面即可，但桌面端要重启宿主才会重新收集注入行。

## 可选配置：给骰子会话单独指定模型

**默认不启用**，骰子会话直接沿用你的默认模型。想让随机事件跑便宜/快的模型时，
在 `%DSH_HOME%\plugins\dsh-lucky-block\config.json` 写（这个字段只能手写，设置面板里没有）：

```json
{
  "model": {
    "provider": "workbuddy",
    "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
    "reasoningEffort": "low"
  }
}
```

`reasoningEffort` 可省略。`provider` / `model` 必须**精确匹配**可用目录里的名字
（目录拿不到时会跳过切换、不影响掷骰子），不确定就先用 `/dice` 命令观察日志。

> ⚠️ **为什么默认关着**：宿主只提供会话级 `sessionController.selectModel`，而它
> 成功后会把这次选择**异步写成 profile 的全局默认模型**。也就是说开启本配置后，
> 第一次掷骰子会顺带把你的默认模型也改成这里写的那个。想恢复就把文件删掉，
> 再在界面里手动把默认模型选回来。

## 用法

| 想干什么 | 怎么做 |
| --- | --- |
| 让 AI 给选择题加幸运方块 | 正常提问，选项末尾自动多一项 |
| 抽一次零成本的（弹窗/蓝屏/签/冷知识/笑话） | **左键单点**方块 / 打 `/dice` |
| 抽一次要花 token 的（论文/新闻/待办） | **长按**方块挖到碎裂 / 打 `/dice` |
| 不满意，回去 | 说「回滚」或打 `/rollback` |
| 方块按钮固定住不挡路 | 右键方块 → 锁定（或双击）；锁定后仍可单点/长按触发 |
| 让方块贴边 | 把它拖到离屏幕边缘 48px 以内松手，自动吸附 |
| 改设置 | 右键方块 → 设置… |

**单点零成本、长按才花钱**：单点只在单击池里抽（五个事件全是本地/视觉，
不建会话、不调模型）；长按只在长按池里抽（三个事件都会开新会话调模型）。
单点是手滑也会发生的动作，所以它不该有成本。

长按阈值 1.4 秒（`lib/client.js` 的 `BREAK_MS`）。按住时手指挪动超过 5 像素即判为
「在拖动按钮」并取消挖掘——所以拖位置和挖方块不会打架。松开或移开都会取消挖掘，
纹路和挖掘声**立刻**一起停。

音效从宿主的 `/dsh-lucky-block/sound/*.ogg` 按需取（16 个原版音节，共 142 KB），
**不内联进客户端 bundle** —— `lib/client.js` 是每次页面启动都要下载的入口，
为只在长按瞬间才用到的音效把它撑大 4 倍不划算。挖掘声每 210ms 一个、4 个变体随机轮播
（只听一个会明显「卡带」），挖穿那一刻再叠一声碎裂音；同时最多 6 个 Audio 元素，
页面切到后台自动静音。

松手吸附（`SNAP_THRESHOLD = 48`）只在**真的拖动过**时生效：鼠标只是滑出方块边缘
（会触发 `pointerleave`）不会吸附，按下就松手也不会。锁定状态下完全不吸附 —— 锁定
就是不建拖动状态，自然短路。吸附有 160ms 的 `left/top` 过渡，视觉上是滑过去而不是瞬移。

方块按钮位置与锁定状态存在浏览器 localStorage（键 `dshLuckyBlock.block`），换机器不跟。

## 出错了怎么看

方块头顶的气泡**只在报错时出现**（正常触发的进度、成功、会话 ID 都不写了 ——
有视觉表演的事件自己会演，没表演的由新会话内容承担反馈）。报错时气泡里是宿主
翻译过的**人话**，点一下可以关掉，例如：

| 情况 | 气泡说什么 |
| --- | --- |
| 插件本体没激活（改动 `lib/` 后没重启） | 插件没有注册这个接口，通常是插件本体未激活：重启 dsh 后再试 |
| 登录态过期 | 宿主拒绝了请求（未登录或登录已过期），刷新页面后重试 |
| 默认工作区被删/移走 | 默认工作区目录不存在或已被移动。请在 dsh 里重新确认默认工作区路径后再试 |
| 工作区不可写 | 没有权限写入工作区（被系统或沙箱拦下了） |
| `config.json` 里的模型不在目录里 | 模型不可用：config.json 里指定的 provider/model 不在可用目录中 |
| 都不是 | 意外错误：<宿主的原始信息> |

想看完整堆栈就翻宿主日志（`dsh` 标准输出）——那边始终打的是原始错误。

> 音效**不会**报错。拿不到音效文件、浏览器拦截自动播放、没有可用音频设备 ——
> 这些一律静默忽略。音效是锦上添花，为它弹一个红色报错气泡是本末倒置。

## 目录

- `lib/index.js` —— 宿主侧（Node）：选项注入、答案识别、回滚、幸运方块事件（分单击/长按两个池）、默认工作区会话创建、可选模型切换、人格层与状态机、本地语料库、音频清单、设置读写、音效文件投放、错误翻译。
- `lib/client.js` —— 客户端（浏览器）：可拖拽幸运方块按钮（含边缘吸附、锁定）+ 单击/长按分流 + 长按挖掘裂纹 / 碎裂粒子 / 音效 + 音频播放 + 弹窗表演 + 蓝屏屏保 + 设置面板 + 台词气泡。
- `lib/persona.js` —— 随机事件的人格层（纯函数，可单测）：默认人格、覆盖合并、人格段拼装、任务正文保护、收尾点评请求。
- `lib/jokes.js` —— 本地笑话库加载器（读 `jokes-data.json`，带 BOM 剥离与只读一次缓存）。
- `lib/jokes-data.json` / `lib/trivia-data.json` —— 本地语料库。
- `lib/audio-tracks.json` —— 音频事件清单（现在是空数组，填上就开始抽）。
- `lib/audio/` —— 音频文件目录，由宿主 `/dsh-lucky-block/audio/<file>` 投放。
- `lib/sounds/` —— 16 个原版 Minecraft 音效（`.ogg`，共 142 KB），由宿主按需投放。
- `cordis.patch.yml` —— 把宿主侧插件插进插件树（客户端那半由 `package.json` 的 `dsh.client` 自动加载）。

## 素材出处

方块面与裂纹是原版 Minecraft 像素素材，以 base64 data URI 内联在 `lib/client.js` 里
（静态 bundle 的 `require()` 只认包 id、不认相对路径，所以不做成独立模块）：

| 素材 | 尺寸 | 来源 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 方块面 | 16×16 | `alexsocha/luckyblock` mod 的 `lucky_block.png` |
| 挖掘裂纹 10 帧 | 16×16 ×10 | 原版资源包 `PixiGeko/Minecraft-default-assets` 的 `assets/minecraft/textures/block/destroy_stage_0..9.png` |

裂纹用 `image-rendering: pixelated` 保持硬边，长按时按进度切到下一帧，最后一帧之后碎裂。
之所以找原素材而不是手绘：手绘的裂纹再怎么调都像程序生成的线条，和那张像素方块贴图
放在一起会突兀；换成原版的黑褐裂纹 + 白色反光碎屑，才是游戏里挖方块的样子。

音效是 Minecraft 1.20.1 原版 assets（`dig/stone1..4.ogg`、`random/break.ogg`），
经 `tools/build-sounds.mjs` 从 mcasset.cloud 镜像取到 `lib/sounds/`。版权归 Mojang Studios；
本插件只作本地开发期素材镜像，**运行时不依赖网络**。

默认性格是机器客服口吻 + 音量梗 + 人体数据冷知识，靠语气和句式传达。
实现里刻意**不提任何作品名、角色名或制造商**，也不靠名字塑造性格 ——
`persona-check.mjs` 有多条断言盯着这一点。

开发期工具（`tools/`，安装运行不依赖）：
`host-smoke.mjs` 跑宿主侧回归（含音效路由与白名单）、
`persona-check.mjs` 人格层单测（真 import）、
`snap-check.mjs` 吸附纯函数（从 `client.js` 抽源码跑，不会与实现漂移）、
`config-check.mjs` 配置读取（含 BOM 坑）、
`local-check.mjs` 本地语料库与分流、
`verify-sounds.mjs` 音效文件 ↔ 客户端清单 ↔ 宿主白名单三方一致性、
`list-events.mjs` 打印事件清单与概率、
`merge-trivia.mjs` / `merge-jokes.mjs` 语料合并器（`--check` 只体检不写盘）、
`build-corpus-overview.mjs` 重新生成 `lib/语料库总览.md`

plugins.description: Selection-annotation plugin for DSH Web (X-WIDE fork of @changfenhuang/dsh-annotation v1.4.11, MIT): color studio, annotation outline, session-scoped clear-all, row-anchor marks, self-check pill.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-xwide-annotation > **X-WIDE fork** — `dsh-xwide-annotation` is a derivative of [@changfenhuang/dsh-annotation](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-annotation) v1.4.11 (by **omdsh-dev**, MIT), adding the **color studio** and the **annotation outline**. Upstream notice and MIT terms are retained verbatim in [LICENSE](./LICENSE). > > 📖 **Usage guide (with screenshots)**: **[docs/USAGE.md](./docs/USAGE.md)** · 简体中文：**[docs/USAGE.zh-CN.md](./docs/USAGE.zh-CN.md)** — quick start, outline panel, color studio, self-check pill, FAQ.
**English** · [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

Selection-annotation plugin for DSH Web: select text → annotate → press Enter to send it along with your message; the model replies to each annotation by number.

🌐 Live Product Site — Explore dsh-annotation in DSH

**Current UI (v1.5.6)** ![Two floating pills: color studio 🎨 and annotation outline 📋](./docs/img/10-floating-pills.png) ![Annotation outline strip — numbered entries per chat](./docs/img/11-outline-strip.png) ![Color studio panel: swatches, custom colors, self-test switch](./docs/img/12-color-studio-panel.png) ![Self-test badge: pill with live event counter](./docs/img/13-badge-pill-live.png) ![Self-test details: mount / style / contrast / hit-area numbers](./docs/img/14-selftest-detail.png)

Select any text in an assistant reply to annotate it (the annotation body may be left empty = just mark the passage). Annotations accumulate across messages and turns. An **Annotations ×N** chip appears next to the input box — hover to view all annotations, remove them one by one. Press Enter and the annotation block goes to the model together with whatever question is in the input box. **The annotation block never shows up as text in your own message bubble** — only the question plus the chip (content visible on hover; hidden before paint, zero flicker). The model replies with `Annotation 1: …` … `Annotation N: …`, one per annotation, and every Annotation label in the reply is a hoverable chip showing the annotated passage and your note. Form: official **bundle plugin** (`dsh.bundle` + a `dsh.client` declaration in package.json, injected into the browser via client-modules; the Node half is an empty implementation). **Zero core changes** — no DSH files are touched; `cordis.patch.yml` only inserts its own id once, and the profile patch stays `[]`. ## Features Sidebar file annotations (DSH 0.1.6-alpha.1): select plain text, Markdown, or code in a workspace file preview and use the same annotate, save, and Enter-to-send flow. The editor and model-facing quote include the file path. After reloading and reopening the original file, its markers are restored; identical passages in different files remain separate. PDF, images, and HTML inside iframes are not covered. | Feature | Description | |---|---| | Select-to-annotate | Select assistant text → toolbar "Annotate" → write your note (may be empty); dismiss by clicking elsewhere or pressing Esc | | Numbered marker + highlight | A blue numbered marker + highlight anchored to the passage, viewport-anchored with collision avoidance, never lost when scrolled out of view | | Cross-turn collection | Any number of annotations accumulate across messages/turns, numbered from 1 | | "Annotations ×N" chip | Small chip beside the input box; hover shows every annotation, deletable individually | | Enter sends with your message | Annotation block + the question in the input box are sent to the model together (the model receives the full content) | | Hidden in your bubble | The annotation block is removed from your bubble's DOM the moment you send (before the browser paints), leaving only the question + the chip (hover to view); historical messages self-heal after a refresh | | Numbered reply correspondence | A format instruction is injected into the message so the model replies `Annotation 1: …` … `Annotation N: …` one by one | | Reply annotation chips | `Annotation N:` in the reply renders as hoverable chips showing the passage + your note | ## Interaction flow ``` Select assistant text ──▶ Toolbar "Annotate" ──▶ Write note / save empty ──▶ Blue numbered marker + highlight ▲ │ └────────────── any number, accumulate across turns ◀────┘ │ ▼ "Annotations ×N" chip beside the input (hover to view / delete) │ Press Enter ▼ Model receives: annotation block (number + passage + note) + your question Your bubble: question only + "Annotations ×N" chip (zero flicker) Model reply: Annotation 1: … Annotation 2: … (hoverable chips) ``` ## Install (official bundle path · the only one) ```sh # Public npm package (works without an npm account) dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-xwide-annotation # Or install directly from the public GitHub source dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/XWIDE/dsh-xwide-annotation.git # local path install (development / debugging) cd /path/to/dsh-annotation dsh plugin --profile web add . # restart the web service — see "Restarting the web service" below ``` To add it only as a Node dependency in an existing project: ```sh npm install dsh-xwide-annotation ``` > `npm install` only adds the dependency; it does not register the plugin with DSH. Use `dsh plugin add` above when installing it into DSH. ### Migrating from the old `@omdsh-dev` package name If you installed the plugin before v1.4.2, remove the old dependency before installing the renamed package: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web remove @omdsh-dev/dsh-annotation dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-xwide-annotation ``` If `dsh web` still fails and mentions `@omdsh-dev/dsh-annotation`, remove only the stale `dsh-annotation` entry that uses that old name from `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`. The plugin now supplies the `dsh-xwide-annotation` entry itself. | Do | Don't | |----|------| | Only `dsh plugin add` / only write `bundles` | **Never** insert the same id again in the profile/home `cordis.patch.yml` | Self-check: ```sh dsh --profile web --dump-config | rg "id: dsh-xwide-annotation" # must be exactly 1 line dsh web --no-open # open the printed one-time token URL in a browser ``` In the browser console, `window.__DSH_BOOT__.entries.find(({ id }) => id === 'dsh-xwide-annotation')` must return an entry with a `url`. dsh 0.1.2 no longer exposes the old bare per-plugin URL. ## Restarting the web service Pick the command for your platform: ```sh # macOS (launchd) launchctl kickstart -k "gui/$(id -u)/com.dsh.web" # WSL / Linux with systemd user services # The unit name may differ by install method; check with: # systemctl --user list-units | rg dsh systemctl --user restart dsh-web ``` Environments without a service manager (e.g. some containers) often need **no restart at all**: `client.js` is served per request with no caching, so a hard refresh (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R) picks up plugin changes. plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

> **Release compatibility:** The current tested Host is official `0.2.0-rc.2`. SeekTTY `1.3.0` is paired with that Host. See the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md) for changes and installation, and the [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md) for exact package evidence.

SeekTTY

A terminal workspace for DeepSeek Harness.

Overview · Quick start · Clarify and Plan · Features · Compatibility

English · 中文

--- ## Overview Run `deepseek` from a project directory to use the native Agent, Session, model, permission, Settings, Profile, plugin, and persistence services of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) in one terminal workspace. SeekTTY is the terminal surface; Harness remains the owner of runtime state. Models, Providers, Agent Presets, permissions, commands, tools, Settings, Skills, MCP servers, and marketplace sources are discovered from the running Harness. Capabilities added by upstream or third-party Bundles therefore appear without being hard-coded into SeekTTY. For requirements that still need definition, the optional [Clarify Host plugin](https://github.com/Hilbert-beinghappy/dsh-plugin-clarify) adds a guided `/clarify` workflow. It asks focused questions, updates a reviewable Draft after each answer, and returns the accepted Draft to the composer. Harness-native `/plan` can then turn the submitted requirement into an implementation plan. ## Development checkout Build and install a local SeekTTY package from the repository root: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm run build pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false ./seektty-1.3.0.tgz dsh --profile tui ``` Use the local tarball for source development and testing. For the released package, use the exact npm version below. ## Quick start Install the published SeekTTY release on its verified official DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 dsh --profile tui ``` These commands install the prebuilt Bundle through native `dsh plugin` reconciliation. The per-command pnpm option avoids the pnpm 11 Global Virtual Store layout that the Cordis loader in the currently tested dsh releases cannot reliably load. SeekTTY never changes global pnpm configuration. Clarify and Auxiliary Runtime are optional, not default dependencies; their historical joint acceptance is listed under [Compatibility](#compatibility-and-verification). The exact `seektty@1.3.0` npm package is documented in the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### Bare `deepseek` launcher After installing `dsh`, install the same SeekTTY release globally and pin Profile reconciliation to its exact npm version: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 export SEEKTTY_SPEC=seektty@1.3.0 deepseek ``` PowerShell uses the same exact npm spec: ```powershell pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false 'seektty@1.3.0' $env:SEEKTTY_SPEC='seektty@1.3.0' deepseek ``` `deepseek` requires `dsh` on `PATH`, or `DSH_BIN` pointing to its executable. Common launch forms include: ```sh deepseek "check this project" deepseek --cwd ../project deepseek --resume deepseek --resume deepseek --profile team-tui deepseek --version deepseek --update ``` `deepseek --update` is self-first: it checks SeekTTY before dsh, installs at most one compatible component per run, and never installs an untested gap or future Host. `DSH_BIN`, local installs, and `SEEKTTY_SPEC` overrides are left unchanged. Update failures do not block startup. Set `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=check` for a post-session notice or `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=0` to disable checks. SeekTTY `1.3.0` supports official dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` and brings more native workflows into the terminal. See the bilingual [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [complete PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### What's new in 1.3.0 - Access native Session actions, plans and artifacts, MCP resources, Team information, schedules, timed/continued questions, and account/model information from the terminal. - Browse Host workspace files with text/binary views and available file watching. Plugins can add terminal Session actions and guarded draft input activities with undo. - Install optional Creator, Browser, or Computer companion Bundles when you need them. With the official voice-input Bundle enabled, `/speech wav` provides reviewed WAV transcription; it does not record from the microphone. - Fix current-Host preset/forms/tool-result handling, stale targets, approval display, watcher cleanup, and bounded shutdown. Keep native Harness ownership and the existing terminal workflows. The release notes also fill gaps in the `1.2.6` summary: Agent Tree navigation, semantic transcript copying, target-specific context menus, Provider configuration, VS Code theme discovery, independent appearance controls, native scrollback, and long-session rendering fixes. Those features were already shipped; the [audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md) identifies their original PRs and versions. ## Interface | DeepSeek light | DeepSeek dark | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek light start screen](assets/seektty-tui.png) | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek dark start screen](assets/seektty-tui-dark.png) | | TypeScript in the light interface | Tools, file reads, and Diff in the dark interface | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY light TypeScript syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-light.png) | ![SeekTTY dark tool and Diff syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-dark.png) | Full mode uses a fixed alternate-screen viewport and keeps the composer and status at the bottom. Its mouse support browses history, selects text, and clicks existing controls inside SeekTTY. F3 or `/mouse native` switches while idle to terminal-native mode: SeekTTY leaves the alternate screen, writes the complete loaded conversation to ordinary terminal scrollback, disables mouse reporting, and lets the terminal or tmux own scrolling, search, and selection. Backfill is sequential and reports progress; Esc stops it without stopping the Session, while Ctrl+L refreshes only the active tail. `/transcript` opens transcript browsing and `/transcript replay` explicitly writes the available conversation again. Images use a textual attachment row in native mode. Already-written history is not recolored or reflowed by SeekTTY; the terminal owns that history. An empty session now opens with a responsive Fastfetch-style welcome page rather than sendable task suggestions. The default uses a packaged, original-color DeepSeek pixel whale plus runtime facts from the current Profile; it does **not** execute Fastfetch. The first-time API-key prompt remains higher priority and finishes before option

plugins.description: 面向 DeepSeek Harness（dsh）Web GUI 的搜索插件，挂在内置右侧栏，不依赖 dsh-better-sidebar。 关键词模式搜文件名与文件内容，支持包含/排除 glob、大小写、正则与类型筛选，命中结果边搜边返回； 代码图模式通过 codegraph CLI 查符号并展开调用方/被调方。命中处高亮，点击即在编辑器中跳到该行。
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-codegraph-search [![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-codegraph-search)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-codegraph-search) A Search tab for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) web GUI's **built-in right sidebar** — no `dsh-better-sidebar` required. One panel, two modes: - **Keyword** — search file **names** and **contents** in the current session's workspace, grouped per file with line numbers. - **Code graph** — query symbols by name / qualified name and expand their callers and callees. Clicking a hit opens the file in the built-in text preview, jumping to the line. ## Modes **Keyword** - File names and content lines; per-file groups with match counts, collapsible. - **Progressive results**: the host streams each file group over NDJSON the moment it is found (`POST /workspace-search/search` with `stream: true`), so hits appear while the walk is still running and the status line counts up live. Rendering is throttled — the first rows show immediately, then the list is updated at most once per 250 ms — so a fast walk never re-renders per file, and the final list is sorted exactly like the buffered response. Code-graph queries stay a single buffered response. - Matched text is highlighted: the query inside file names, matched lines, and code-graph symbol names / signatures, using the same matching rules the search itself used (literal case folding, or the regex and `Aa` state). - VS Code-style filters: **files to include / files to exclude** (comma-separated globs, supports `**`, `*`, `?`, `{a,b}`), `Aa` case toggle, `.*` regex toggle. - Type filter: quick extension chips (`.ts .tsx .js .py .json .md`) plus a free-form extension field. - Skips hidden files/dirs, `.git`, `node_modules`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `dist`, `build`, `.next`, `target`, symlinks, binary files, and files over 1 MiB. **Code graph** - Needs the `codegraph` CLI on the server and a `codegraph init`-ed workspace (the index lives in `.codegraph/`). - Symbol results show kind, signature and location; each row lazily expands callers / callees. Missing CLI, missing index, timeout and parse failures are reported with their own message and a copyable fix command. ## Usage - The panel scopes to the **current session's workspace** automatically. - `Enter` searches; results also refresh ~250 ms after a filter or mode change. - `Esc` clears the query. - Switching tabs no longer re-runs the search: results, scroll position and expansion state are preserved. ## Requirements - dsh web (the built-in right sidebar, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right`) - Node.js >= 22 - `codegraph` CLI — only for the code graph mode ## Install Published on npm as [`dsh-codegraph-search`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-codegraph-search): ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-codegraph-search ``` From a local checkout instead — the profile then keeps it as a `link:` dependency, so your edits take effect on the next restart: ```sh git clone https://github.com/Wilyte/dsh-codegraph-search.git dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-codegraph-search ``` Either way the plugin is added to the `web` profile's bundle list, so **restart dsh web** to load it. No extra sidebar plugin is needed: the tab registers directly with dsh's built-in right sidebar, and the sidebar's guide page shows a "Code search" entry. ## Configuration All fields optional (profile patch layer, `id: code-search`): ```yaml - id: code-search config: maxFiles: 5000 # hard cap on files scanned per search maxMatches: 300 # hard cap on total content matches maxLineLength: 300 # hard cap on one reported line maxFileBytes: 1048576 # files above this skip the content scan codegraphBin: codegraph # CLI used by the code graph mode codegraphTimeoutMs: 15000 codegraphMaxResults: 50 ``` Every cap is reported honestly in the status line ("file scan truncated" / "matches truncated") instead of silently dropping results. ## How it works Dual-face bundle. - **Host half** (`lib/index.js`) registers an HTTP route on dsh's `webServer` (`ctx.webServer.register`, prefix `/workspace-search`) — `POST /workspace-search/search` and `POST /workspace-search/graph`. It deliberately does **not** inject `connection`: that service does not exist in the web host profile. - **Client half** (`lib/client.js`) registers a tab type on `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` (kind `search`), renders its body into the keyed `sidebar.right.pane.tab` seat, and contributes a guide-page entry. Copy is routed through the Client locale service (zh/en) and the stylesheet is mounted through `ctx.effect`, using the GUI's own design tokens. ## Credits This plugin started from [dsh-workspace-search](https://github.com/AmmiWang/dsh-workspace-search) by [AmmiWang](https://github.com/AmmiWang) — the original VS Code-style keyword search tab for dsh, then docked in [dsh-better-sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar). The code graph mode, streamed results and the built-in right sidebar were added on top of it. Thanks for the original work. ## License MIT

plugins.description: A DSH plugin: collect pending ask_user_question prompts from other sessions and answer them without leaving the current one.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-sideask

See and answer `ask_user_question` prompts from other DSH sessions, without leaving the one you are in.

**Powered by [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)** — a plugin, not a fork.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

## The problem

DSH renders an `ask_user_question` card only in the session that asked it. If you are working in session B while session A is blocked on a question, you cannot see it. Your choices are to switch sessions and hunt for it, or to leave the asking agent waiting.

## What this plugin does

- Collects pending questions from every session in the workspace.
- Shows a small **待答 N** counter in the sidebar footer. It is not rendered at all when nothing is pending.
- Opens a compact panel at the bottom-left corner when clicked: one card per session, showing the session title, the question, its options, and a free-text field.
- Submits the answer back to the asking session through `userQuestions.answer`.

The panel never takes over the composer, never steals focus, and never covers the center of the page.

## Requirements

- DSH `0.2.0` or later.
- **`ask_user_question` must run in `timed` mode.**

That last point matters. In the default `blocking` mode, a question stays in a foreground wait that only the card in the asking session can settle. This plugin cannot answer it — no external interface can. In `timed` mode the wait expires, the tool returns `pending`, and the question becomes *continued*: still answerable, but no longer owned by one interface. That is the state this plugin picks up.

Configure it on the `tool-ask-user` row of your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: tool-ask-user
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
  config:
    mode: timed
    timeout: 60
```

With that in place, a question becomes answerable from this panel after `timeout` seconds. The tool also accepts a per-call `timeout` argument, so a caller that wants it faster can pass a smaller number.

## Install

1. Put the package under your profile's plugin directory, for example
   `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/plugins/dsh-sideask`.
2. Link it into the profile's `node_modules/@local` under a name that matches the package name:

   ```powershell
   New-Item -ItemType Junction `
     -Path  "$HOME\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\@local\dsh-sideask" `
     -Target "$HOME\.dsh\profiles\desktop\plugins\dsh-sideask"
   ```

3. Add the row to `cordis.patch.yml`:

   ```yaml
   - id: dsh-sideask
     name: '@local/dsh-sideask'
   ```

4. Restart DSH. Client plugins are bundled at boot; reloading the page is not enough.

## How it works

Two halves.

**Host half** (`index.js`) listens to `session/event` globally and keeps a map of pending questions keyed by `sessionId|callId`.

- On `tool/call` named `ask_user_question`, it records the call with its questions and the session's working directory.
- On `tool/result`, it inspects the result: a `pending` reply means the timed wait expired and the question is still answerable, so the record is kept. Any other result means the question was settled, so the record is dropped.
- `turn/end` does not clear records; a continued question outlives the turn that asked it.

Two HTTP routes:

- `GET /dsh-sideask/list?session=<id>` returns the pending questions whose working directory matches the requesting session's, so one workspace stays separate from another.
- `POST /dsh-sideask/answer` with `{ sessionId, callId, answers }` forwards the answer via `ctx.userQuestions.answer(agent, callId, { answers })`.

**Client half** (`client.js`) registers two slots:

- `sidebar.footer.action` — the counter button, hidden when the count is zero.
- `shell.overlay` — the panel, positioned bottom-left, dismissed with × or Esc.

It polls the list route every 4 seconds while the counter is mounted, and refreshes on open.

## Gotchas worth knowing

- `userQuestions.answer` takes `{ answers: [...] }`, not a bare array. A bare array is rejected and returns `false`.
- `stillOpen === true` means the answer was accepted into the agent's queue. `false` means no matching continued question was found.
- A `pending` tool result is not an answer. Treating it as one makes questions disappear from the panel before anyone has answered them.
- After a successful submit, remove the item from the local cache immediately. Waiting for the server to drop it leaves a window where the panel still lists an answered question.

## Known limitations

- Only questions from the same working directory are shown.
- A question that is still inside its foreground wait cannot be answered from here; see Requirements.
- Records live in memory. A DSH restart clears them; questions that are still answerable will not be re-listed until they are asked again.
- Records older than 24 hours are dropped from the list.

## License

MIT

# dsh-starry-sky-theme

A dark-only starry-sky theme for **DeepSeek Harness** (DSH) Web UI: a deep-space palette, a slowly twinkling starfield, and faint constellation figures behind the interface.

![Starry Sky icon](./icon.svg)

## Features

- **One sky for both appearance settings.** Light and Dark both resolve to the night sky. The Client half pins the appearance preference to `dark`, so picking *Light* in Settings → Appearance is corrected back to *Dark* while the plugin is enabled.
- **Deep-space palette.** Navy-violet surfaces, moonlit text, and a starlight-blue accent applied as an alias-token layer.
- **Constellation figures.** Four faint star-chart polylines with glowing anchor stars, drawn in the same sky as the twinkling stars.
- **Quiet by design.** The sky sits in the frame-wide click-through overlay: no pointer capture, no layout shift, and it honours `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Removable.** Disabling the plugin removes the palette layer and the sky in the same HMR pass, and stops pinning the appearance.

## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.1-rc.2` (Web UI).
- No extra dependencies: the Client half uses only the `react` module the Harness already provides.

## Install

From the **Plugin Market** (once listed): Settings → Plugins → Plugin Market → Themes, choose *Starry Sky*.

Or install the package into a profile directly:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-starry-sky-theme
```

Then reload the page. The plugin activates immediately; no restart is needed for the Client half.

## Use

- Open Settings → Appearance: the plugin keeps the appearance on **Dark**. The Light choice is available in the stock UI but snaps back while the plugin is enabled.
- To choose Light again, disable the plugin in Settings → Plugins (or remove it). The saved preference stays `dark` until you change it.
- To turn the sky off, disable the plugin; the original palette returns immediately.

## How it works

The Client module registers three things:

1. `theme.overrideTokens('<package id>', tokens)` — an alias-token layer with the dark value repeated for both color schemes, composed over the active theme and removed when the plugin is disposed.
2. A `theme/change` listener that calls `theme.setTheme('dark')` whenever the resolved scheme is light, so both appearance settings stay night.
3. `slots.register('shell.overlay', ...)` — a `pointer-events: none` sky layer rendered above every column. Stars are generated deterministically (seeded PRNG), constellation lines are fixed percentage coordinates, and the twinkle is CSS keyframes (disabled under reduced motion).

No DOM outside the component is touched, no other plugin's styles are read, and no session state is modified.

## License

MIT © 2026 Nektropy

## 中文简介

DeepSeek Harness 的深色星空主题：深空底色、缓慢闪烁的星点，以及四组淡淡的星座连线。浅色与深色外观都被统一为深色——插件启用时会把外观固定在深色，选择「浅色」会被自动改回。关闭插件即移除配色层与星空，并停止固定外观。支持 DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.2` 的 Web 界面。
